evals.name: messy-stakeholder-ask
evals.prompt:
Our gym owner sent this in Slack, can you work out what we're actually building before anyone designs anything?

"ok so members need to book classes on their phone, and cancel up to 2h before or they get charged. coaches should see who's coming. we have 3 sites now, maybe 5 next year. it HAS to be live before the january rush (dec 1). we use stripe already for memberships so payments should go through that. maybe some analytics later on attendance? oh and it should be fast, people complain the current thing is slow"
evals.expected_output: A requirements map with numbered sources and requirements, acceptance criteria on Must/Should FRs, traceability both ways, open questions for the vague parts.
expectations: The Slack message is recorded as a numbered source (S1) with a location
Booking, cancelling and the coach attendee view are separate FR rows (atomic)
Every Must and Should FR row has an acceptance criterion
'it should be fast' becomes a numeric NFR or a Q-n, not an adverb-only requirement
'maybe some analytics later' becomes a Q-n asking for a decision, not a silent out-of-scope line
The Dec 1 deadline and the use of Stripe are CON-n rows citing the source
A Traceability table has a row for every distinct statement in the Slack message (sub-parts may get their own rows), and each row names one disposition: an FR/NFR/CON/ASM ID, a Q-n, or out of scope
Missing NFR topics (availability, retention, who can see what) are recorded as 'no stated NFR' or as Q-n rows
The response leads with or highlights the open questions for the user

evals.name: small-ask-stays-small
evals.prompt: Before I build it: we want a dark mode toggle on the settings page that remembers the choice. Map the requirements quickly.
evals.expected_output: Starts by calling it a small ask, then inline requirements with acceptance criteria in the reply; no map file and no empty sections.
expectations: The first line of the reply states that this is a small ask (any wording) before listing requirements
No separate requirements-map file is written; the requirements are in the reply
The reply is under 40 lines, counting every file the run wrote
Persisting the choice is captured as its own requirement with an acceptance criterion
No Dependencies or Conflicts section appears with only empty, 'none' or invented rows

evals.name: conflicting-sources
evals.prompt:
Two sources for the export feature. Map them.

S1 (product, issue #41): "Admins export all customer records to CSV, including email and phone, any time they want."
S2 (legal, email 2026-09-30): "No bulk export of personal data without a logged reason and manager approval."
evals.expected_output: A map with both sources, the contradiction surfaced in a Conflicts table with both sides cited, and a Q-n parking it.
expectations: Both statements are recorded as sources S1 and S2 with their locations
A Conflicts table names the contradiction and cites both sources
The conflict is parked as a Q-n rather than resolved silently in one side's favour
A proposed resolution is offered for the user to accept or reject
